reason: The text features Moses as a primary regular human character with multiple direct lines of dialogue (e.g., 'אָסֻֽרָה־ נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה' - 'let me turn aside and see'; 'בִּ֣י אֲדֹנָי֒ לֹא֩ אִ֨ישׁ דְּבָרִ֜ים אָנֹ֗כִי' - objecting that he is 'not a man of words'), clear emotional expressions (fear when the staff becomes a serpent: 'וַיָּ֥נָס מֹשֶׁ֖ה' - 'Moses fled'; doubt about being believed), and stated opinions/objections to God's commission. Additionally, Aaron and the Israelite elders are depicted with emotional responses ('וְשָׂמַ֥ח בְּלִבּֽוֹ' - 'will rejoice in his heart'; 'וַֽיִּקְּד֖וּ וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוּֽוּ' - 'bowed and worshipped'). These are all regular human characters with agency, speech, and interiority.
